original_question: Can one prove a short-time existence theory for the inhomogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann equation with hard potentials and algebraically decaying initial data? The open case singled out in the paper is hard potentials gamma > 0 with initial data behaving like f_0 <= <v>^{-q}.
target_in_paper: Section 3, “On the existence of solutions,” specifically the unnumbered paragraph stating that no documented short-time existence result covers the inhomogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann equation with algebraically decaying initial data in the hard-potential regime gamma > 0. This is the nearest official formulation in the paper; it is not presented there as a numbered conjecture. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core target quite well: it identifies the inhomogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann equation, the fact that the issue is short-time/local Cauchy theory rather than global existence, the hard-potential regime gamma > 0, and the missing algebraic-decay case typified by f0(x,v) ≲ ⟨v⟩^{-q}. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))
missing_details: The paper frames this as an unnumbered open gap in Section 3, not as a formal numbered conjecture or theorem; that should be made explicit to stay paper-faithful. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))

A stand-alone version should name the actual Cauchy problem: the inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation ∂t f + v·∇x f = Q(f,f) with initial datum f(0,x,v) = f0(x,v). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))

The collision operator should be identified as the standard non-cutoff Boltzmann operator with kernel of the form (2.3), i.e. the usual inverse-power-law non-cutoff class parameterized by gamma and the angular singularity exponent s. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))

The desired result should be identified as a short-time classical/local-in-time existence theorem for generic smooth data, not a perturbative near-Maxwellian result and not a global theorem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))

Your draft mentions algebraic decay but not the additional regularity needed for a classical solution; the paper leaves the exact function space implicit here, so a faithful stand-alone formulation should at least say 'for sufficiently smooth initial data' or 'in a natural weighted regularity class.' ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))

The exponent q should not be left completely free in a sharpened formulation; the question should say 'for some sufficiently large q' or equivalently in the weighted class natural for local theory. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))

The draft does not specify the spatial/velocity variables x and v, nor that the decay is in the velocity variable. The paper’s notation ⟨v⟩ uses the Japanese bracket convention introduced earlier. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))

To mirror the paper’s exact intent, the question should contrast this open hard-potential/polynomial-decay regime with the existing hard-potential Cauchy theory that requires Gaussian decay and the polynomial-decay local theory available only for soft potentials. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))

Nearby context also matters: Theorem 3.1 shows that once a classical solution exists and suitable hydrodynamic bounds hold, extra rapid initial decay is only imposed there in the non-hard regime gamma + 2s ≤ 0, which helps explain why the short-time existence step for hard potentials with polynomial tails is the sharp unresolved case. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))

Algebraic metadata such as ambient ring/field, homogeneity degree, or nilpotency conditions are not relevant to this PDE paper; the missing stand-alone ingredients are instead PDE-specific data: variables (t,x,v), collision kernel, decay class, regularity class, and the local-in-time quantifier. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))
refined_question: For the inhomogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann Cauchy problem ∂t f + v·∇x f = Q(f,f), with the standard inverse-power-law non-cutoff collision kernel B(|v-v*|,cosθ) of the form (2.3) and in the hard-potential regime gamma > 0, can one prove a short-time classical existence theorem for generic sufficiently smooth initial data whose velocity decay is only polynomial, for example f0(x,v) ≲ ⟨v⟩^{-q} for some sufficiently large q, instead of the Gaussian velocity decay required by the currently documented hard-potential Cauchy theory? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))
justification: This rewrite is as close as possible to the paper’s actual intent because the paper does not state a numbered conjecture here; rather, Section 3 isolates a precise gap in the short-time theory: Gaussian-decay local theory is available for hard potentials, polynomial-decay local theory is available for soft potentials, but the hard-potential/polynomial-decay case is not covered by any documented result. The refined version therefore makes explicit the Cauchy problem, the standard non-cutoff kernel class (2.3), the local/classical nature of the desired theorem, and the fact that the decay is only polynomial in v, while avoiding broader claims about global existence, weak solutions, or conditional regularity. The nearby Theorem 3.1 further clarifies that, once a classical solution exists under hydrodynamic control, hard potentials are not the regime where extra rapid initial decay is imposed there, which is why the short-time existence problem with algebraic tails is the sharp paper-faithful formulation of your draft. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2204.06401))
